edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Illic igitur et Scripturarum et expositionum adulteratio deputanda est, ubi diversitas doctrinae invenitur. Quibus fuit propositum aliter docendi, eos necessitas coegit aliter disponendi instrumenta doctrinae. Alias enim non potuissent aliter docere, nisi aliter haberent per quae docerent. Sicut illis non potuisset succedere corruptela doctrinae sine corruptela instrumentorum ejus; ita et nobis integritas doctrinae non competisset sine integritate eorum, per quae doctrina tractatur. Etenim quid contrarium nobis in nostris? quid de proprio intulimus, ut aliquid contrarium ei quod esset in Scripturis deprehensum, detractione, vel adjectione, vel transmutatione remediaremus? Quod sumus, hoc sunt Scripturae ab initio suo; ex illis sumus, antequam aliter fuit, antequam a vobis interpolarentur. Cum autem omnis interpolatio posterior credenda sit, veniens utique ex caussa aemulationis, quae neque prior, neque domestica unquam est ejus quod aemulatur, tam incredibile est sapienti cuique, ut nos adulterum stylum intulisse videamur Scripturis, qui sumus et primi et ex ipsis, quam illos non intulisse, qui sunt et posteri et adversi. Alius manu Scripturas, alius sensus expositione intervertit. Neque enim si Valentinus integro instrumento uti videtur, non callidiore ingenio, quam Marcion, manus intulit veritati. Marcion enim exerte et palam machaera, non stylo usus est; quoniam ad materiam suam caedem Scripturarum confecit. Valentinus autem pepercit; quoniam non ad materiam Scripturas, sed materiam ad Scripturas excogitavit: et tamen plus abstulit, et plus adjecit, auferens proprietates singulorum quoque verborum, et adjiciens dispositiones non comparentium rerum.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, there the corruption of Scriptures and of explanations must be reckoned, where diversity of doctrine is found. To those who had proposed to teach otherwise, necessity compelled to arrange otherwise the instruments of doctrine. For they would not have been able to teach otherwise, unless they had otherwise the things through which they taught. Just as to them the corruption of doctrine could not have succeeded without the corruption of its instruments; so also to us the integrity of doctrine would not have been fitting without the integrity of those things through which doctrine is treated. For what is contrary to us in our own things? What have we introduced of our own, so that we might remedy something contrary to what was in the Scriptures, by subtraction or by addition or by transmutation? What we are, the Scriptures are from their beginning; we are from them, before it was otherwise, before they were interpolated by you. But when every interpolation is to be believed as later, coming certainly from a cause of rivalry, which is neither prior nor domestic to what it rivals, it is so incredible to every wise person, that we seem to have introduced an adulterous style into the Scriptures, who are first and from them, as that they did not introduce it, who are later and opposed. One person corrupts the Scriptures with his hand, another corrupts the sense with explanation. For not even if Valentinus seems to use an intact instrument, did he not introduce his hand into the truth with a more cunning intellect than Marcion; Marcion indeed used openly and publicly the sword, not the style; since he made the slaughter of the Scriptures for his material. Valentinus however spared; since he did not devise the Scriptures for his material, but devised his material for the Scriptures: and yet he took away more, and added more, taking away the properties of each of the words, and adding arrangements of non-comparable things.

choices.why: conveys the sense of competition or emulation

pass_b_english: So that is where you have to locate the corruption of Scripture and its interpretation -- right where divergent doctrine shows up. People who set out to teach something different were forced to retool the instruments of doctrine, because they could not teach differently unless they had different tools to teach with. Just as their doctrinal corruption could not have succeeded without corrupting its instruments, so our doctrinal integrity would not be possible without the integrity of the means through which doctrine is handled.

What exactly is the case against us in our own writings? What private material have we ever introduced to fix something contrary to Scripture by subtracting, adding, or transposing? The Scriptures are what we are from their very beginning; we come from them, before anything was otherwise, before you interpolated them. Since every interpolation is by definition later, springing from rivalry -- a rivalry that is neither prior nor native to the thing it rivals -- it is absurd to any wise person that we, who are first and derived from Scripture, should be accused of foisting an adulterated style onto it, while they, who are later and opposed, are not.

One man corrupts Scripture with his hand, another corrupts its sense with his explanation. Even if Valentinus appears to use an intact text, he did not lay hands on the truth with any less cunning than Marcion. Marcion wielded a butcher's cleaver openly, not a pen, because he slaughtered Scripture to supply his own material. Valentinus spared the text, but only because he did not devise Scripture for his material; he devised his material for Scripture. Yet he subtracted more and added more, stripping away the proper force of each word and inserting arrangements of things that do not compare.

review.notes: All clauses in the Latin source were checked against Pass A and Pass B. Pass A is a faithful literal translation. Pass B is a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between Marcion's 'machaera' (cleaver/sword) and Valentinus's 'stylo' (pen/style), and the causal distinction regarding their relationship to the 'materia'.
